purpose: Record falsifier and downgrade-condition coverage for C1 boundary-rewriting domains and selected C2 source-maintenance domains that most affect Human Infra subject-continuity claims.

scope.c1Coverage: all one-hop C1 boundary-rewriting research domains with README and AGENTS files
currentLimitations: This is priority-domain coverage, not full coverage of every C2 domain.
This register records falsifier and downgrade scaffolding; it does not complete Source Cards for every domain.
This register does not validate external evidence or prove any intervention works.

entries.strongClaim: Future waiting routes may reduce the subject's experienced waiting cost only when time differential, life support, exit, continuity and adoption conditions all hold.

falsifiers.condition: No plausible exit, communication or recovery path is specified for the waiting route.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to speculative narrative and block model entry
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: scenario card with exit, communication, recovery and abort gates

falsifiers.condition: The route preserves external time difference but destroys subject continuity or agency.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: continuity card covering memory, cognition, embodiment and governance

prohibitedUses: 不证明现实工程可行性
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create route cards for future waiting, biostasis, and metric-redshift variants with exit and continuity gates.

entries.strongClaim: Longevity evidence can enter Human Infra only after the route exposes intervention, comparator, endpoint, evidence level, access, adoption and risk gates.

falsifiers.condition: The route has only mechanism plausibility or animal data without human endpoint, safety or applicability boundary.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: keep as candidate route and prohibit lifespan conclusion
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: source card distinguishing mechanism, animal, biomarker, clinical endpoint and long-term safety

falsifiers.condition: The route improves a biomarker while worsening function, safety, access, or opportunity cost.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade from longevity claim to mixed-effect or negative route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: route card with positive and negative chains plus prohibited-use boundary

prohibitedUses: 不提供药物或补剂建议
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Extend LEV route cards to non-mainstream boundary routes and connect each route to a falsifier row.

entries.strongClaim: Biostasis can only be treated as a future-waiting preservation hypothesis if structure, damage, revival, identity and governance uncertainties are explicitly gated.

falsifiers.condition: The preservation process causes unrecoverable information loss in structures required for identity or agency.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: structure-preservation evidence and identity-critical information boundary

falsifiers.condition: Future revival is assumed without specifying required repair, validation and governance conditions.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: revival-condition card and non-claim boundary

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build Source Cards separating structure preservation evidence from revival and continuity claims.

entries.strongClaim: Brain preservation and emulation claims must prove enough information preservation, readout, interpretation and identity continuity before they can represent subject continuity.

falsifiers.condition: The preserved data cannot support memory, personality, agency or functional reconstruction claims.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to anatomical archive, not subject-continuity route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: information sufficiency card covering structure, dynamics and functional validation

falsifiers.condition: The route produces a copy claim but cannot defend continuity of the original subject.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: identity theory boundary and governance note

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create a brain-information sufficiency matrix covering structure, dynamics, memory trace, validation and identity theory.

entries.strongClaim: A disembodied CNS route can only count as subject-continuity research if it maintains living neural function, agency-relevant cognition, sensory-motor interface and rights/governance conditions.

falsifiers.condition: The system maintains tissue viability but cannot preserve conscious agency, communication or welfare.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as organ-support artifact, not subject-continuity route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: agency and welfare criteria with abort conditions

falsifiers.condition: Interface, sensory input, or motor output failure prevents the subject from acting or choosing.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: interface redundancy and agency-output card

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Separate viability, consciousness, agency and governance requirements into independent abort gates.

entries.strongClaim: Memory editing can affect subject continuity only when benefits to trauma, learning or identity stability are separated from risks of identity disruption, coercion and evidence loss.

falsifiers.condition: The intervention improves distress metrics but damages identity coherence, agency, testimony, or consent integrity.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: benefit-risk card covering memory function, identity, consent and social misuse

falsifiers.condition: The claim lacks a clear target memory, mechanism, reversibility and governance boundary.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: target-mechanism-reversibility-governance table

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build a memory intervention boundary table separating therapeutic, enhancement, coercive and evidentiary contexts.

entries.strongClaim: Accelerating returns and technology convergence can affect subject continuity only if discovery speed, validation, translation, access and governance all improve enough to change real technology-window probabilities.

falsifiers.condition: Discovery or prediction speed increases but validation, translation, safety or access does not improve.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: route card separating discovery, validation, translation, deployment, access and safety gates

falsifiers.condition: A single-domain exponential trend is used to claim system-wide medical, social or governance acceleration.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: block C1 boundary-rewriting claim and require domain-specific evidence
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: multi-domain convergence matrix with independent evidence and negative cases

prohibitedUses: 不把未来学时间表写成事实
不证明长寿逃逸速度已经实现
不把自动科研速度替代临床或治理证据
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Promote AI automated science Source Cards into a technology-window convergence matrix with positive, negative and correction-risk rows.

entries.strongClaim: Recursive self-improvement can be treated as a boundary-rewriting hypothesis only when AI contribution to AI R&D, iteration compression, feedback quality and oversight latency are explicitly evidenced and gated.

falsifiers.condition: AI improves isolated coding or benchmark tasks but cannot materially improve model design, training, evaluation or deployment pipelines.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to ordinary automation or C3 tool augmentation
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: AI-RD task evidence separating code assistance, experiment design, model improvement and deployment autonomy

falsifiers.condition: Iteration speed increases while oversight, interpretability, evaluation and rollback capacity fall behind.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as risk-amplifying recursive route, not net-continuity gain
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: oversight latency and abort-gate evidence for recursive development loops

prohibitedUses: 不提供自主复制或逃逸监管路径
不把代码生成等同于智能爆炸
不把递归增强自动写成正收益
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build an AI-RD automation evidence table connecting METR-style task horizons to self-improvement depth and oversight latency.

entries.strongClaim: Singularity-scale systems can only be treated as subject-continuity infrastructure if control, interpretability, rollback, distribution and governance boundaries remain strong enough to preserve human future choice.

falsifiers.condition: System benefits depend on outputs that humans cannot explain, test, reproduce, contest or roll back in time.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as opaque high-risk infrastructure and block positive continuity claim
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: interpretability, reproducibility, audit, rollback and incident-response evidence

falsifiers.condition: Control of compute, data, models, interfaces or distribution is concentrated such that subjects lose practical choice or access.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade from human-infra gain to governance-and-distribution risk
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: power, access, opt-out, accountability and distribution-control assessment

prohibitedUses: 不提供绕过安全或监管的方法
不把 AI 风险叙事替代事实证据
不把不可解释系统自动写成可接受基础设施
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create Source Cards for AI control, interpretability, incident reporting, system cards and frontier model governance.

entries.strongClaim: Superhuman intelligence becomes a Human Infra boundary condition only when technical systems exceed human capability across consequential domains and alter what humans can understand, choose or reach.

falsifiers.condition: Capability evidence is limited to narrow benchmarks, demos or isolated expert tasks without robust cross-domain transfer.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to C3 capability augmentation signal
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: task coverage evidence comparing models, human experts, organizations and real-world deployment constraints

falsifiers.condition: The system exceeds human performance but remains fully reviewable, controllable and bounded to local use cases.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: keep as high-capability tool rather than C1 boundary-rewriting threshold
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: capability, autonomy, tool access, reviewability and external impact assessment

prohibitedUses: 不把单个模型榜单写成超人智能
不提供危险能力扩散方法
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build a capability-threshold matrix separating benchmark superiority, expert replacement, cross-domain transfer and external boundary impact.

entries.strongClaim: Cellular reprogramming may reset aspects of cell age only if rejuvenation can be separated from identity loss, tumor risk and system-level disruption.

falsifiers.condition: Age markers improve while cell identity, tissue function, or cancer safety worsens.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to biomarker-only or unsafe mechanism claim
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: paired age, identity, function and safety endpoints

falsifiers.condition: Evidence remains in vitro or animal-only but is written as human healthspan extension.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: species, tissue, delivery, endpoint and follow-up boundary

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Convert the Yamanaka-factor literature spine into Source Cards with identity-loss and tumor-risk gates.

entries.strongClaim: Regenerative medicine contributes to subject continuity only when replacement or repair improves durable function without unacceptable immune, tumor, integration or access risks.

falsifiers.condition: Anatomical repair does not translate into durable function, independence or effective time.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade from continuity gain to structural surrogate
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: functional endpoint and follow-up evidence

falsifiers.condition: Integration, immune, manufacturing or cost constraints prevent realistic access.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: implementation and access card

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build route cards separating cell therapy, tissue engineering, organ replacement and local repair.

entries.strongClaim: Cancer control protects subject continuity only when early detection, treatment access, overdiagnosis, mortality benefit and functional burden are jointly assessed.

falsifiers.condition: Screening increases detection without reducing mortality or preserving function.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: mortality, stage, false-positive, overdiagnosis and function endpoints

falsifiers.condition: Follow-up or treatment access is missing after detection.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: screening-to-treatment pathway evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create screening route cards that include mortality, overdiagnosis, follow-up and access gates.

entries.strongClaim: Immune maintenance supports subject continuity only when protection, inflammation control, immune surveillance and autoimmunity risks are balanced.

falsifiers.condition: Immune activation improves one marker while increasing chronic inflammation, autoimmunity, or tissue damage.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: benefit-harm profile across infection, inflammation, autoimmunity and cancer surveillance

falsifiers.condition: Evidence ignores age, frailty, exposure context or immune heterogeneity.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade from general maintenance claim to context-limited claim
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: population and immune-state stratification

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Map immune-aging source cards into infection, inflammation, surveillance and autoimmunity channels.

entries.strongClaim: Neuro-continuity is a source-maintenance condition because subject continuity fails if memory, cognition, agency, self-model or communication irreversibly collapse.

falsifiers.condition: A route preserves biological survival but not memory, agency, communication or self-continuity.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as biological survival without subject continuity
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: neurocognitive and identity-continuity endpoints

falsifiers.condition: Enhancement or intervention improves a narrow task while degrading judgment, autonomy or long-term safety.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to local task gain with continuity risk
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: task, autonomy, side-effect and long-term safety evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create variables for memory, executive function, agency, communication and identity-continuity risk.

entries.strongClaim: Mitochondrial bioenergetics matters for subject continuity only when cellular energy signals connect to organism-level function, fatigue, recovery and disease risk.

falsifiers.condition: Cellular or biomarker improvement does not translate into fatigue, function, recovery or disease endpoint improvement.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: linked biomarker-to-function evidence

falsifiers.condition: Intervention increases oxidative stress, toxicity, or maladaptive energy demand.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as unsafe or mixed-effect energy perturbation
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: dose, safety, function and adverse-effect evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build a biomarker-to-function map for mitochondrial claims.

entries.strongClaim: Genomic stability and DNA repair contribute to subject continuity only when reduced damage or improved repair lowers cancer, cell failure or tissue dysfunction without increasing malignant escape.

falsifiers.condition: Repair-pathway manipulation improves damage markers but increases cancer, clonal expansion or genomic instability.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: cancer, clonal, repair-fidelity and long-term safety evidence

falsifiers.condition: The claim treats DNA repair as universally beneficial without tissue, age, dose or pathway context.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: pathway-specific and tissue-specific evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Separate damage reduction, repair fidelity, senescence, apoptosis and cancer escape into distinct variables.

entries.strongClaim: Biological age clocks are observation tools for model feedback only if they predict function, risk, intervention response or endpoints without being mistaken for lifespan itself.

falsifiers.condition: Biomarker age changes do not align with function, disease, mortality or recovery endpoints.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: endpoint-alignment and intervention-response validation

falsifiers.condition: The clock is used for individual death dates, medical decisions, ranking or discrimination.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: use-case boundary and no-individual-prediction audit

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create a biomarker validation matrix separating correlation, prediction, intervention response, endpoint alignment and misuse.

entries.strongClaim: Proteostasis and autophagy support subject continuity only when protein quality-control changes improve function, resilience or recovery without causing toxicity, wasting or failed clearance.

falsifiers.condition: Autophagy or proteostasis markers improve while tissue function, strength, cognition or survival-relevant resilience does not improve.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: function endpoint or recovery endpoint linked to protein-quality variables

falsifiers.condition: The route increases catabolism, malnutrition, toxicity, immune stress or cancer-supportive survival of damaged cells.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as mixed-effect or negative quality-control route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: adverse-channel evidence covering wasting, toxicity, immune stress and malignant persistence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build Source Cards separating autophagy flux markers, lysosomal function, tissue-level outcomes and adverse channels.

entries.strongClaim: Senescence clearance can enter Human Infra only when reduced senescent burden or SASP activity improves tissue function while preserving repair, tumor suppression and safety.

falsifiers.condition: A senescence-targeted route clears markers but worsens wound healing, immune defense, tissue repair or frailty.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: downgrade to context-limited or negative route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: repair, infection, wound-healing and frailty endpoint evidence

falsifiers.condition: The claim ignores that senescence can be protective in tumor suppression or tissue remodeling contexts.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: block universal clearance language and require context-specific framing
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: context table separating harmful chronic senescence from protective senescence roles

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create a senescence route matrix separating burden, SASP, tissue context, repair function and tail-risk channels.

entries.strongClaim: Extracellular matrix and glycation routes affect subject continuity only when structural stiffness, fibrosis or crosslink burden can be tied to mobility, vascular function, wound healing or organ resilience.

falsifiers.condition: A route changes matrix or glycation markers without improving mechanical function, perfusion, mobility, wound healing or organ endpoints.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: mechanical, vascular, mobility or wound-healing endpoint evidence

falsifiers.condition: Matrix remodeling increases rupture, impaired healing, inflammation, fibrosis rebound or off-target tissue damage.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: tissue-specific remodeling safety and failure-mode evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build ECM Source Cards linking crosslinks, fibrosis, tissue mechanics and functional outcomes.

entries.strongClaim: Stem-cell reserve and renewal support continuity only when they preserve tissue repair capacity without exhausting niches, inducing dysplasia or increasing malignant transformation.

falsifiers.condition: A route increases proliferation or stem-cell markers without durable functional repair or tissue integration.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: durable repair, differentiation fidelity and integration evidence

falsifiers.condition: Renewal stimulation increases clonal expansion, dysplasia, fibrosis or tumor risk.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: longitudinal clonal, dysplasia, fibrosis and malignancy safety evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Separate reserve, niche, proliferation, differentiation, integration and malignancy variables in Source Cards.

entries.strongClaim: Microbiome ecology affects subject continuity only when microbial changes can be tied to metabolism, immunity, barrier function, inflammation, infection risk or treatment response.

falsifiers.condition: A microbiome association cannot distinguish cause, consequence, confounding, diet, medication or disease-state effects.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: causal design, longitudinal data, intervention evidence or sensitivity analysis

falsifiers.condition: Microbiome manipulation worsens infection risk, immune dysregulation, GI symptoms or treatment safety.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as mixed-effect or unsafe ecological intervention
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: adverse event, pathogen transfer, immune and symptom outcome evidence

prohibitedUses: 不提供益生菌或移植建议
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build microbiome Source Cards separating association, causality, intervention response and safety transfer risks.

entries.strongClaim: Cardiovascular resilience is a core source-maintenance route only when risk-factor control, perfusion, vascular integrity and recovery capacity reduce failure risk without creating harmful tradeoffs.

falsifiers.condition: A cardiovascular route improves a surrogate while failing to reduce events, functional decline, hospitalization or effective-time loss.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: event, function, hospitalization or effective-time endpoint evidence

falsifiers.condition: Risk reduction increases falls, bleeding, hypotension, renal injury, treatment burden or access inequity.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as mixed-effect route with explicit harm channels
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: adverse event, burden, access and subgroup evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Map cardiovascular variables to hazard, function, recovery and treatment-burden outcomes.

entries.strongClaim: Musculoskeletal integrity supports subject continuity by preserving mobility, strength, balance, fracture resistance and task execution capacity under risk and recovery constraints.

falsifiers.condition: A route improves body-composition or imaging markers without improving strength, mobility, falls, fractures, pain or daily function.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: strength, mobility, falls, fracture, pain or ADL endpoint evidence

falsifiers.condition: Training, drug or device pathways increase injury, pain, overuse, frailty, access burden or adherence failure.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as context-limited or negative execution route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: injury, adherence, functional and subgroup feasibility evidence

prohibitedUses: 不提供用药或设备建议
entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create a musculoskeletal variable table connecting strength, balance, fracture risk, pain and task execution.

entries.strongClaim: Nutrition and metabolic health support subject continuity only when energy availability, metabolic risk, body composition and food environment are modeled with safety, adherence and access constraints.

falsifiers.condition: A diet or metabolic route improves a biomarker but worsens energy, mood, function, social feasibility, eating-disorder risk or long-term adherence.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as mixed-effect or unsafe resource route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: function, safety, adherence, burden and subgroup evidence

falsifiers.condition: The route ignores food access, cost, culture, comorbidity, medication interaction or baseline nutritional risk.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: implementation-context and access-equity evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Separate metabolic biomarkers, functional energy, adherence, access and adverse nutrition channels.

entries.strongClaim: Renal and hepatic clearance maintain subject continuity by preserving internal-environment stability, drug handling, toxin removal and metabolic reserve under failure-risk constraints.

falsifiers.condition: A clearance claim lacks kidney/liver function, exposure, medication, comorbidity or acute-failure context.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: renal, hepatic, exposure and treatment-context variables

falsifiers.condition: A route improves one clearance marker while increasing dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, toxicity, bleeding, infection or treatment burden.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: safety, adverse-event, medication-interaction and function evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build clearance Source Cards connecting renal/hepatic variables to homeostasis, toxicity and treatment-safety outputs.

entries.strongClaim: Respiratory oxygenation supports subject continuity when ventilation, oxygen exchange, airway protection, sleep breathing and exposure control preserve energy, cognition and survival reserve.

falsifiers.condition: Respiratory markers improve without measurable gains in symptoms, sleep, cognition, activity, exacerbations or survival-relevant reserve.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: symptom, sleep, activity, exacerbation or reserve endpoint evidence

falsifiers.condition: A route increases device burden, adherence failure, infection risk, CO2 retention, oxygen hazard or access inequity.
falsifiers.downgradeAction: classify as context-limited or negative respiratory route
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: device, adherence, adverse-event and access evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Connect oxygenation, sleep breathing, airway risk and environmental exposure to energy and effective-time outputs.

entries.strongClaim: Blood oxygen transport and hemostasis matter for continuity only when anemia, oxygen-carrying capacity, bleeding, thrombosis and transfusion safety are linked to function and failure risk.

falsifiers.condition: A blood marker improves without improving fatigue, exercise tolerance, cognition, bleeding/thrombotic outcomes or acute-event risk.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: function, oxygen-delivery, bleeding/thrombosis and acute-event evidence

falsifiers.condition: A route reduces one risk while increasing opposing bleeding, clotting, transfusion, immune or access risks.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: risk-balance evidence for bleeding, thrombosis, transfusion and safety

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Build a hemostasis tradeoff map covering oxygen transport, bleeding, thrombosis, transfusion and functional endpoints.

entries.strongClaim: Endocrine regulation supports subject continuity only when hormonal feedback, stress response, metabolism, reproduction, bone, mood and cardiovascular tradeoffs are modeled as a coupled control system.

falsifiers.condition: A hormonal route improves a single lab value while worsening mood, sleep, bone, fertility, cardiovascular risk, cancer risk or feedback stability.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: multi-axis outcome and adverse-channel evidence

falsifiers.condition: The claim ignores feedback loops, age, sex, comorbidity, baseline deficiency/excess, dose or monitoring context.
falsifiers.evidenceNeeded: axis-specific, population-specific and feedback-aware evidence

entries.nextEvidenceAction: Create endocrine axis cards separating deficiency, excess, replacement, suppression, feedback and adverse tradeoffs.

nonClaims: This register does not complete all C2 domain-level Claim-Evidence Matrices.
This register does not prove the scientific correctness of any domain claim.
This register is a local gate that prevents priority-domain claims from existing without falsifier and downgrade scaffolding.
